messages.content: Help me signal the end of an XML element with the qualified name `{namespaceURI='http://www.example.com', localPart='item', prefix='ex'}` and augmentation information `augmentations` in an XML processing application that uses namespaces?

function.name: XMLNamespaceBinder_endElement
function.description: Signals the end of an XML element, handling namespace-related processing if namespaces are enabled, or delegating to the document handler otherwise. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

element.description: The qualified name of the element that is ending. Use QName object, has a constructor that takes in three parameters, namespaceURI, localPart, prefix This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

augs.description: Augmentation information associated with the element. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the tool "XMLNamespaceBinder_endElement" with arguments:

{
    element: ??? (qualified name)
    augs: augmentations
}

But we have to provide the qualified name as a QName object constructed from namespaceURI, localPart, prefix.

The user says: "with the qualified name {namespaceURI='http://www.example.com', localPart='item', prefix='ex'}". So we should pass something like new QName("http://www.example.com", "item", "ex") but since it's just a string representation maybe they want us to construct it accordingly.

Given the instructions: "Use QName object, has a constructor that takes in three parameters, namespaceURI, localPart, prefix." And this parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

Thus we might produce JSON where element field contains something representing the QName. For example: {"namespaceURI":"http://www.example.com","localPart":"item","prefix":"ex"} or perhaps simply "QName('http://www.example.com','item','ex')".

Let's check guidelines: In previous tasks, when calling such functions, you supply the argument values directly; e.g., element: "new QName(...)" etc. But here the instruction says "This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation."

So likely we should send element: "javax.xml.namespace.QName{uri=http://www.example.com, local part=item, prefix=ex}" or similar.

Better to use canonical representation: "QName(\"http://www.example.com\", \"item\", \"ex\")"

Also augs: "augmentations" presumably variable containing augmentation info. We could set augs: "augmentations".

Hence output:

```json
{
   "name": "XMLNamespaceBinder_endElement",
   "arguments": {
      "element": "QName(\"http://www.example.com\",\"item\",\"ex\")",
      "augs": "augmentations"
   }
}
```

Yes. Let's do that.
